'''Mark Yakovlevich Azbel''' ({{langx|ru|Марк Яковлевич Азбель}}; 12 May 1932 — 31 March 2020) was a Soviet and Israeli [[physicist]].<ref>[http://ferro.phys.msu.ru/study/phys/spets/04-4.html Развёрнутая программа спецкурса «Динамические свойства магнитных материалов»]</ref> He was a member of the [[American Physical Society]].

Between 1956 and 1958, he experimentally demonstrated [[Cyclotron motion#Cyclotron resonance|cyclotron resonance]] in metals, and worked out its theoretical basis.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/dn/e_006_06_1126.pdf |title=Theory of Cyclotron Resonance in Metals |access-date=2020-04-05 |archive-date=2018-08-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180827164417/http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/dn/e_006_06_1126.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=o5Yb7Q2t1qIC&pg=PA263&lpg=PA263&dq= Jenö Sólyom «Fundamentals of the Physics of Solids: Volume II: Electronic Properties»]</ref><ref>[https://www.spiedigitallibrary.org/ebooks/FG/Field-Guide-to-Solid-State-Physics/AzbelKaner-Cyclotron-Resonance/AzbelKaner-Cyclotron-Resonance/10.1117/3.2510243.ch49?SSO=1 Azbel – Kaner Cyclotron Resonance]</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=FOOyBgAAQBAJ&pg=PA348&lpg=PA348&dq= Rudolf Herrmann, Uwe Preppernau «Elektronen im Kristall»]</ref>

Azbel's 1964 analysis of Bloch electrons in a magnetic field contained ideas which were prescient of both the renormalization group and (though he did not make this explicit) the possibility of a [[fractal]] that was eventually discovered by [[Douglas Hofstadter]] and later called [[Hofstadter's butterfly]].

==Biography==
Azbel was born in 1932, in [[Poltava|Kharkiv]] (at the time, in the [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic]]) to a family of physicians.<ref>[http://histpol.pl.ua/ru/petrovskij-poltavskij-kadetskij-korpus/personal-ppkk/zakonouchiteli-svyashchennosluzhiteli-ppkk?id=1159 История Полтавы]</ref> From 1941, aged 9 to 12, he and his family lived under wartime evacuation in ([[Siberia]]).

In 1944, the family returned to Kharkiv. In 1948 Azbel graduated from high school and in the same year entered the [[National University of Kharkiv]]. After graduation, he taught mathematics at evening school.

In 1958, he defended his doctorate (Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences) under the supervision of [[Lev Landau]] and [[Pyotr Kapitsa]].<ref>[http://www.ufn.ru/ru/authors/azbel_m_ya/ Статьи, публикуемые на сайте УФН]</ref><ref>[http://www2.tau.ac.il/Person/exact/physics/researcher.asp?id=acjgeedec   Professor Mark Azbel]</ref> In 1964 he began working at [[Moscow State University]] and concurrently as a section chair  at the [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]].

In 1972, Azbel applied for [[emigration]] from the Soviet Union to Israel, and in 1973 (a full four years before leaving the Soviet Union) was appointed a lecturer at [[Tel Aviv University]], where he initially gave his lectures by telephone.

Having been refused exit permission from the Soviet Union, he participated in the movement of [[refusenik]]s in the USSR in the mid-seventies.<ref>Refusenik, trapped in the Soviet Union / Mark Ya. Azbel; edited by Grace Pierce Forbes. Boston: Houghton Mifflin co., 1981, {{ISBN|0-395-30226-9}}</ref> Azbel finally emigrated from the USSR in 1977 and was appointed Professor at [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref>[http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,907505,00.html Education: Physics by Phone]</ref> He lived mainly in Israel until his death in 2020.

== Scientific contributions==
Azbel was a theoretical physicist.  His areas of study included the quantum physics of electrons in metals, and he made the first prediction of cyclotron resonance in metals, now widely known as the Azbel-Kaner resonance.

In an important 1964 article,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Azbel|first=Mark|title=Energy Spectrum of a Conduction Electron in a Magnetic Field|journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics|volume=19|pages=634}}</ref> Azbel made conjectures about the nature of the Harper spectrum which contributed to the discovery of the [[Hofstadter butterfly]] in 1974.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Satija, Indubala I., 1952-|title=Butterfly in the quantum world : the story of the most fascinating quantum fractal|others=Hofstadter, Douglas R., 1945-, Morgan & Claypool Publishers,, Institute of Physics (Great Britain)|date=6 September 2016|isbn=978-1-68174-117-8|location=San Rafael [California] (40 Oak Drive, San Rafael, CA, 94903, USA)|oclc=957689639}}</ref>
